brief: Raymond James' daily chartbook covers five independent items. The S&P 500 Industrials sector has fallen for six straight days, its longest losing streak since 2024, down 13.5% from its Aug. 14 high, led by AI-buildout-linked industries such as Electrical Equipment (-25.6%) and Machinery (-18.6%). RJ calls the selloff overdone and remains constructive, expecting data center and grid construction to continue, aided by lower oil prices. Separately, a typical Thanksgiving dinner for 10 will cost about $59 in 2026, up 6% year over year, the first increase since 2022, driven partly by diesel and fertilizer input costs, though still about 9% below the 2022 peak. On credit, record IG issuance (over $190bn MTD, over $2tn YTD, partly hyperscaler driven) has not widened spreads, which held at 86-92bps. RJ favors higher quality bonds into year end. On the Fed, Chair Warsh calls conditions too easy but not restrictive. Goldman's Financial Conditions Index has since hit its highest since May 2025, suggesting markets are already doing some of the Fed's tightening. RJ frames the S&P's 5.1% weekly drop, 8.2% off its Oct. 6 high, against 16% 2027 consensus EPS growth, a cheaper forward P/E, and an RSI near 31, calling it technically overdone.
